title: Building in the social events economy in 2026
decision: Choose a defensible UK launch wedge across friendship dating talks craft games sport performance hobbies wellness spa retreats and local discovery using non-UK companies only to test transferable mechanisms.

foreignCurrencyReference.usage: Approximate current sterling comparisons rather than historical transaction-date or accounting conversions

Canonical keyword baskets with national and London observations kept separate where overlap is plausible
Current live-web review of operator homepages event listings pricing terms privacy safety and help pages
Primary regulator and government evidence for UK social conditions event risk consumer terms data protection and online safety
SEC filings and official results for public-company revenue and payer evidence

Current-operator census across 52 managed event activity platform institutional and infrastructure examples

Comprehensive national Google Ads screen of 244 adult in-person formats using one non-additive primary phrase plus supporting context for each format
Launch-potential score weighted across primary demand commercial intent repeatability social design operating ease revenue depth and eventisation headroom
Cross-format contribution scenarios with every non-observed price capacity and cost marked as an assumption

Intellectual-nightlife sensitivity model covering event fill break-even city cadence and a ten-city network
Mechanism-level AI-disruption analysis covering generated event content, organiser tooling, synthetic companionship, discovery agents, physical delivery, and provenance

Weighted city-launch scorecard combining two comparable demand measures with bounded operator evidence and explicit confidence, evidence-coverage and largest-unknown fields
Fifteen-city depth screen across 24 leading and strategically important formats using 360 explicit city rows and 360 separate local-geo rows
Comparative city-format liquidity index using equal-weight log-normalized explicit and local-geo demand without adding the overlapping observations

Current twelve-row operator benchmark covering price purchase mode repeat structure evidence supported and evidence not established
Three-city launch-intent screen across eight formats and five separate discovery booking repeat beginner-or-adult and group-or-corporate baskets
One hundred and twenty explicit city-modified intent rows kept separate from one hundred and twenty generic local-geo rows
Current first-party supply and public price review for the leading Manchester Birmingham and Bristol launch cells

limitations: Average monthly searches are rounded trailing historical averages and not obtainable traffic.
Google Ads may group or suppress close variants and zero-return rows are not proof of zero demand.
Friendship discovery phrases include mixed commercial informational and community intent.
Operator scale attendance and satisfaction statements are first-party unless explicitly identified otherwise.
Dinners With Friends publishes inconsistent participation totals and start-date wording across live pages.
Timeleft UK subscription pricing was not visible without account signup.
Capital budgets valuations dilution and operating gates are illustrative scenarios rather than observed offers or market benchmarks.
The 2027 to 2030 cases are scenarios rather than probability-weighted forecasts.
First-party funding and operating claims for private companies are not audited unless explicitly stated otherwise.
The report's interview evidence comes from attributed public sources rather than interviews conducted for this project.
Activity keywords overlap and include family tourist retail informational and commercial intent so they are not summed into a market size.
The 244-format scorecard combines one observed demand signal with structural judgement; it is a prioritisation aid rather than an empirical success probability.
The comprehensive format screen is broad but not literally exhaustive and excludes most child-only professional religious political and purely online formats.
Selected international operators demonstrate mechanisms and are not evidence of UK demand price or transferability.
The operator census is a mechanism map rather than proof that all 52 products are profitable or direct competitors.
Cross-format contribution cases are planning scenarios and should not be read as operator benchmarks.
Liiiv public terms disclose monetisation mechanisms but its live price list take rate active users GMV and revenue remain unknown.
GBP equivalents use one September 2026 reference basis and are not historical transaction-date conversions accounting values or executable rates.
The intellectual-nightlife model assumes every listed direct cost and excludes central overhead founder labour VAT insurance tax and portfolio failures.
Eventbrite AI feature and roadmap statements are first-party platform evidence and do not establish operator economics or attendee outcomes.
The chatbot study is a US adult preprint without a non-chatbot control group and does not establish UK event substitution or willingness to pay.
No first-party AI-assisted event operations, agent-referred booking, attendee, non-returner, host, venue, or repeat cohort was available.
City keyword phrases overlap, contain mixed tourist, family, retail, informational and commercial intent, and do not form a market-size estimate.
The local-geo and explicit-city screens overlap and must not be added; a Google Ads city target is not equivalent to a metro catchment or safe evening-travel boundary.
The selected city operator sample is not an exhaustive competitor, venue, host or event-supply census.
Seed Talks city totals are first-party cumulative claims with unknown paid share, capacity, refunds, period consistency, repeat and contribution.
The city scorecard excludes current venue terms, customer-acquisition cost, retention, contribution, host supply, transport constraints and founder-specific local advantage.
The 24-format city depth is a staged comparison rather than an exhaustive city screen of all 244 national formats.
City-format liquidity scores are normalized comparison indexes and are not percentages market shares market sizes or forecasts.
Retreat demand is often destination practitioner and audience led so city-modified and city-targeted search can understate or mislocate purchase intent.
Deep-score decision ceilings are explicit research judgement rather than measured probabilities of commercial success.
Fill-sensitive economics use assumed capacities direct costs and blended ticket yields and exclude VAT central overhead founder labour insurance tax and failed-event portfolio losses.
Operator price pages show current purchase options but do not establish attendance utilization wholesale partner terms retention or profit.
The launch-intent screen covers eight formats and three cities selected from the wider ranking rather than every format-city combination.
Intent baskets and geography methods overlap; their relative shape is diagnostic and not a customer funnel conversion rate or market share.
The acquisition sensitivity assumes 90 percent event fill, repeated paid attendance and a 50 percent allocation of lifetime direct contribution to acquisition; none is observed.
A ten-search rounded row is too thin for a dependable acquisition forecast even when Google returns a nominal CPC.
Public venue prices exclude activity-specific permissions availability staffing equipment cleaning catering licensing insurance and signed cancellation terms.
The risk-and-controls register is research guidance rather than legal safety insurance tax or licensing advice.
